evidence.note: Anthropic's own documentation: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that uses tools. It does not settle whether that counts as 'neurosymbolic'.

reviews.rationale: Whether Claude Code is 'neurosymbolic' turns on a label with no agreed definition. No evidence can settle the claim, so it is not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own judgement in his own post.

contract.note: The plain reading (no clear AI-driven improvement visible by June 2026) is ordinary and fair. Revenue and EPS still grew, so the result depends on that reading. Slower growth was partly expected in the September 2025 outlook.

reviews.rationale: By June 18, 2026, growth had slowed from 7% to about 3%, bookings had fallen, the outlook missed estimates, and the stock had its worst day on record. No AI-driven step-up was visible. Revenue and EPS growth, plus outside causes such as the Middle East conflict, make the picture weaker, but they do not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: By June 2026 Accenture's growth had slowed, and management described large AI programs as early-stage. There was no sharp, AI-credited jump in growth or margins. Some AI progress is reported, but it falls short of the transformation Accenture promoted in September 2025.
